question: A shopkeeper marks up his goods by 30% and then gives a discount of 10% on the marked price. Apart from this, he uses a faulty balance which reads 1 kg for 870 g. What is his net profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Multiplier = (**Markup Factor**) × (**Discount Factor**) × (**Weight Factor**)

Net Multiplier = (130 / 100) × (90 / 100) × (1000 / 870)

Net Multiplier = 1.3 × 0.9 × (100 / 87) = 1.17 × (100 / 87) = 117 / 87 = 39 / 29

Profit % = [(39 − 29) / 29] × 100 = (10 / 29) × 100 ≈ 34.48%

**∴ The correct answer is 34.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Markup** = 30%, **Discount** = 10%, **Faulty weight** = 870 g instead of 1000 g.

**Formula Used:**

Net Profit % = [(Total SP / Total CP) − 1] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/819023e39fe0f72c1f6f9700fdcca510fa4e9779b78b0e9876db0273bb152c77.png] 

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 g of goods be ₹1.

⇒ **Actual CP** for the shopkeeper (for 870 g) = 870 × 1 = ₹870.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** for 1000 g = 1000 + 30% of 1000 = ₹1300.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** after 10% discount on MP = 1300 − (10 / 100) × 1300.

⇒ **SP** = 1300 − 130 = ₹1170.

⇒ **Net Profit** = SP − CP = 1170 − 870 = ₹300.

⇒ **Net Profit %** = (300 / 870) × 100.

⇒ **Net Profit %** = (30 / 87) × 100 = (10 / 29) × 100 ≈ 34.48%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit % due to weight fraud = [True Value − False Value] / False Value × 100. In this case, (1000 − 870) / 870 × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Relationship: SP = CP × (1 + Markup %) × (1 − Discount %). This represents the **price multiplier** effect.

Successive Percentage Change

The effective percentage change for two successive changes x% and y% is [x + y + (xy / 100)]%.
